decision_58: the element of a signature is (lhs holder + value class, rhs holder + value class) -> answer token, keyed by the input cell form_a|vc_a|form_b|vc_b so that it crosses a language boundary through the shared layer-1 value classes
decision_60: a backend refusal is the token 'refuse:codegen'; an ABSENT element is silence and carries no token
dee_ruling: each row isnt a row element. its a vector
that way something like php.== cant appear to have obtained god-operator status.
format:
SPARSE, three tables and one vector per leaf.
  cells[i]   the element key, form_a|vc_a|form_b|vc_b
  tokens[i]  one answer token
  values[i]  one element VALUE: the sorted list of token
             ids a leaf's holders carried at one element
  leaves[k].vec  a flat list of pairs [cell id, value id],
             sorted by cell id.  A cell id ABSENT from the
             list is an element the leaf is SILENT on: it
             was never asked, and that is not a token.
Reading one leaf back is therefore
  {cells[c]: [tokens[t] for t in values[v]]
   for c, v in leaves[k].vec}
grain_flag: FLAGGED, OVERTURNABLE.  the owner has not chosen between the holder-pair grain and the form-pair grain.  The holder-pair grain is the default because it is the literal reading of `each row isnt a row element, its a vector' and because it is the stricter of the two.  Every count is published under both.
